SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Prove correctness. Then earn the scale.

A gated backlog with named ownership, dependencies and measurable exit evidence.

Proposed pilot design

This page describes a target design. The local lab and browser models demonstrate bounded subsets; the proposal is not production acceptance. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

Passing the lab earns the next tests

The single-host lab demonstrates the core sharing and authority rules. A bank pilot still needs authenticated regional services, crash and partition recovery, migration of normalized tables, approved placement and retention, and measured capacity. The backlog below separates these decisions and their required evidence.

Planning estimate, not a delivery commitment

An indicative 12–14 week path assumes an experienced cross-functional team, available infrastructure and timely approvals. Start with approved 100k parties / 200k relationships and one business workflow. The 50M/100M performance rehearsal is a separate synthetic-data exercise. The items below are proposed work, not completed controls.

Sequence the risk reduction

01Decide · weeks 1–2

Approve field footprint, traffic, authority freshness and pilot scope.

02Foundation · weeks 2–5

Regional HA, identity, indexed access and common local transactions.

03Correctness · weeks 4–8

Epochs, durable delivery, safe deltas, audit and purge.

04Prove · weeks 6–11

Full-scale synthetic data, open-load tests, fault and migration rehearsals.

05Pilot · weeks 12–14+

Read-only shadow, one workflow canary, measured go/no-go.

Pilot exit criteria

GateRequired evidence
Residency and entitlementNo unauthorised payload or customer-linked metadata in excluded stores, queues, logs or restore targets.
Business integrityAtomic business/hook rollback, idempotent replay, parent closure and concurrent-writer tests pass.
AuthorityStrict or approved bounded remote-read contract implemented; no stale-epoch resurrection; fail closed on lost authority.
PerformancePer-operation/cell p95/p99 targets at agreed peak for 60 minutes; 24-hour normal soak; errors and load-generator drops included.
RecoveryAZ and authority loss tested; 30-minute receiver outage drains in ≤60 minutes at design incoming rate with revocation priority.
OperationsSigned runbooks, on-call drill, regional evidence, restore quarantine and controlled rollback.
Business releaseApproved capped population, shadow reconciliation, 1% → 5% → 25% canary with hold points and named rollback owner.

For implementers: engineering brief
HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Operational isolation decision: use three regional work classes: authority guard, operational delivery and bulk reconciliation. Separate relay paths, queues/topics, worker groups, connection/concurrency budgets and retry/quarantine paths. A policy transaction advances scoped authority and creates a guard intent plus one reconciliation cursor; it must not enumerate affected rows. Operational commits remain local ACID with outbox/audit/idempotency. Operational priority never bypasses current policy. Source restriction commit, remote enforcement and physical convergence are separate milestones. Read the Work isolation page before implementing any queue or policy change. The interactive lab and admission specification are synthetic; the v3 database harness still has its original process lock and serial worker.

Use the published capacity model as an explicit hypothesis, never as a database benchmark. Target 50M parties, 100M relationships and the supplied typed child-table distribution. Normal workload is 10k reads/s + 1k writes/s; design peak is 30k reads/s + 5k writes/s globally. Preserve geography, entitlement, purpose and explicit-deny semantics. Use the scale/ scripts and measured workload aggregates to replace assumptions. The v3 runtime remains a PoC with full scans and a process lock; no optimized production data path has been implemented.

Convert P01–P24 into a pilot backlog while preserving dependencies and exit evidence. Validate team capacity and environment availability before promising dates. Start with read-only shadow and capped approved population. Keep security, migration, HA and performance gates explicit. Stop rollout on any sovereignty leak, stale authorisation or material SLO breach; perform the rehearsed rollback. Do not treat simulated performance as pilot acceptance.
